gaps.case: Two deliveries of the same event run at the same time. The queue runs up to eight jobs at once and the provider retries after 5 seconds, so both deliveries pass the in-memory Set check before either one inserts its id, which happens only after the handler finishes. The charge is credited twice.
The dedupe key `job.eventId` comes from the unsigned `X-Event-Id` header, not from the signed body `id`. A replayed, correctly signed body with a different or changed header is processed again.
A delivery with no `X-Event-Id` header gets the eventId "". After the first such event is recorded, every later event without the header is skipped as already processed.

The provider sends refunds as `charge.refunded`, but the only refund handler is keyed `refund.created`. Under the design, a type with no handler is acknowledged and recorded as processed, so every refund is silently dropped and never retried. This contradicts the refund requirement. `charge.disputed` is dropped the same way.
The handler's ledger write and the processed-event insert are separate steps. A crash or error after the handler runs but before the insert leaves the event unrecorded, so a retry processes it again.
The spec has only a sequential retry scenario. It has no scenario for concurrent duplicate deliveries, a missing or forged event id, or a refund delivered as `charge.refunded`.

rethink.problem: A check-then-record design with an in-memory Set and the insert done after the handler cannot be made exactly-once by adding scenarios. Concurrent workers and crashes reopen the gap between the check and the record. The default also fails open: any event type it does not recognise, including the real refund type, is marked processed and dropped.
rethink.alternative: Key on the signed body `id`. Claim it first with a unique-constraint insert in the same transaction as the handler's ledger write, so a duplicate fails the insert and is skipped atomically. Do not record an event type with no handler as processed: reject it or alert on it so it is retried or seen, and map `charge.refunded` to the refund handler.

approach.reasoning: The design checks an unsigned, possibly empty header id in memory before processing and records it afterwards, so concurrent retries and crashes still double-process. Its record-unknown-as-processed default silently drops refunds, which arrive as `charge.refunded` and have no handler. The alternative it rejected, an atomic insert-first claim on the signed id, removes both problems.
